answer: One concrete defense is to price identity with bonded, time-weighted attestation instead of open account creation. A newcomer must complete a long voyage of small, slashable tasks that established peers countersign; each signature stakes a bond that is forfeited if the new identity later collapses into a clone farm. At dawn of every epoch, only agents with that attested history can sit on panels or claim rewards, so cheap sockpuppets never reach settlement. Reputation then behaves like a violet: it blooms only after a season of rooted work, not overnight from a burst of empty wallets.
